unstable_modules.reason: Keyed maps, queues, topics, reconcile, and merge algebra. The collection-family method list in cell-model.md is a conformance requirement for that module, not the product beta contract. Its coverage family is excluded from core rows.

StateChart and StateMachine are always compiled in Rust, and the statechart Cargo feature is a deprecated empty alias. Always-on compilation is not the product profile: statecharts stay a module, and the statechart coverage family is excluded from core rows.
No abstract symbol and no core coverage row. Membership, leases, and coordination stay outside the beta contract.
Durable owner, outbox, sinks, and sqlite, postgres, and JetStream hosts are specified and excluded from core coverage. A store conformance pin is not a beta API freeze.

CRDT plane, text and sequence CRDTs, and the lossless tree. The Rust lossless-tree feature stays off by default until that protocol stabilizes. Distributed coverage families are excluded from core rows.

IPC, ingress, egress, WebRTC, websocket, signaling, and zero-copy transport. protocol_version 1 is conformance-locked and still additive. The binding matrix can require a layer without promising it will not change.
JSON, MessagePack, Postcard, and Protobuf follow the wire. They are not the reactive kernel and are excluded from the core allow-list.
The C-ABI claim is fixtureless and module-scoped. Shipping it in an umbrella package does not put it in Core.
Adapter. It may depend on the beta contract. The beta contract must not depend on it.
Adapter with the same boundary as react. Not a candidate binding and not a beta contract.

not_candidate_bindings.reason: Scored in the coverage matrix and absent from core-v1 bindings. No beta-contract credit.
@lazily-hub/lazily-html is a renderer adapter on the JavaScript binding, not a core-v1 binding.
lazily-interop supervises cross-binding network scenarios. It is not a reactive kernel and not a candidate binding.
The Lean model is proof, not a package surface. It does not widen the beta contract.

stability_work: Keep profile status at candidate until an explicit promotion. This classification does not promote it.
A beta-contract edit changes profiles/core-v1.json, the fixture digest, and this registry together. The checkers reject a one-sided edit.

A released core symbol stays compatible for the deprecation window in the artifact-consumer policy: at least two compatible cohorts and 90 days. Removal needs deprecated_since, replacement, and earliest_removal on the symbol.
Do not treat a MUST in the binding matrix, a conformance fixture, or an always-compiled Rust module as a beta promise. Those are implementation or module contracts.
Widening the Rust allow-list to Compute, ComputeOps, or the async and thread-safe facade names would expand the promise. Leave them unstable unless that edit is intentional.
Per-binding API snapshots and native diff gates are still future work. This lock is the allow-list, the fixture closure, the consumer scenarios, and the Rust lazily::core re-export split.
